# `run-graph` skill, `install skills` installs every bundled skill, and the `to-tasks` hand-over ## What to build After `to-tasks` writes the task folder, the user should be able to say "start the run" and the coding agent does it. Add a bundled skill `skills/run-graph/SKILL.md` that works out the arguments, runs `npx graph-execution --spec --provider

--web` from the repo root, reports by exit code and **stops** (never polls, sleeps, fetches the URL or reads `.graph-execution/`). Change `graph-execution install skills` to install every skill folder under the package's `skills/` (so `to-tasks` and `run-graph`), deciding the refusal per skill folder per destination: an existing `to-tasks` no longer blocks installing a missing `run-graph`. The command prints one line per installed skill and one per skipped skill (with the `--force` hint) and exits 2 only when nothing was installed and something was skipped. Finally the last step of `skills/to-tasks/SKILL.md` offers to start the run. ## Context: files to read before implementing - `src/install/skills.ts` (all) — `INSTALL_TARGETS`, `DESTINATIONS`, `SKILL_SOURCE = /skills/to-tasks/`, `installSkills` (refuses everything when any destination exists), `InstallError`. - `src/cli.ts` (lines 149–164) — the `install skills` command prints `Installed to-tasks skill into ` per destination; `main()` prints thrown errors as `error: …` with exit 2. - `src/install/skills.test.ts` (all) — existing expectations: default target `agents` → `.agents/skills/to-tasks`; refusal on a second run with exit 2 and stderr containing `already exists`; `--force` overwrites and removes stale files; the test "installs nothing when only one of two destinations exists" encodes the OLD all-or-nothing rule and must change; "the bundled skill" tests check `skills/to-tasks/SKILL.md` content (frontmatter, `.agents/tasks/.json`, `validate-tasks.mjs .agents/tasks`, no HITL/AFK). - `skills/to-tasks/SKILL.md` (frontmatter and last section "6. Validate the task files", ending with the `npx graph-execution .agents/tasks --spec --provider …` command) — the text to extend. `.agents/skills/to-tasks/` and `.claude/skills/to-tasks/` are identical copies in this repo; keep all three in sync. - `package.json` (`files` contains `skills`) — packaging is already covered. - `docs/prd/01-run-skill-and-web-view.md` §6 (copy of the spec the run receives) — the skill's required wording: frontmatter, steps 1–5, exit codes 0/2/3. ## Patterns to follow **Skill frontmatter and voice:** look at `skills/to-tasks/SKILL.md` top: `---\nname: …\ndescription: …\n---`, imperative second-person instructions, fenced command blocks. **Frontmatter to use:** ```yaml name: run-graph description: Start a graph-execution run of a task folder in the background and open its live view in the browser. Use when the user wants to run, start or execute the tasks created by to-tasks, or asks to "run the graph". ``` **Filesystem tests:** temp dir per test (`mkdtemp(path.join(tmpdir(), "ge-install-"))`), assertions on `readdir` sorted names; CLI tests run `dist/cli.js` with `execa(..., { reject: false })`. ## Step-by-step tasks ### CREATE `skills/run-graph/SKILL.md` (and copies) - **IMPLEMENT**: the skill body, in this order: 1. *Work out the arguments.* Tasks folder: the one `to-tasks` just wrote in this conversation, else `.agents/tasks` if it exists, else ask. Spec: the PRD used to make the tasks in this conversation, else ask; never guess between several files. Provider: what the user said; otherwise default to the agent's own CLI (Claude Code → `claude`, Codex → `codex`, OpenCode → `opencode`, Qwen Code → `qwen`) and say so; any other agent: ask. Pass `--concurrency`, `--model` and `--no-merge` only if the user asked. 2. *Warn, don't block, about uncommitted code.* If `git status --porcelain` shows changes outside the tasks folder and the spec, tell the user that agents only see committed code and ask whether to continue or commit first (the task folder and spec don't need to be committed). 3. *Launch.* `npx graph-execution --spec --provider

--web` from the repo root (`graph-execution` directly if installed globally). 4. *Report and stop, by exit code, never by matching output.* **0**: give the user the URL the CLI printed and tell them: the run is in their browser and can be aborted there; a failed node can be retried from its page (click the node, read the AI summary, press Retry); when the review is clean the result lands as uncommitted changes on the current branch, on top of whatever they edit meanwhile, with overlaps as conflicts; `graph-execution open` brings the page back; `graph-execution --resume --web` continues an interrupted run. **Then end the turn: do not sleep, poll, fetch the URL, read `.graph-execution/`, or tail logs.** **3** (hand-off blocked): give the user the printed command to run in their own terminal, then stop; don't work around the sandbox. **2**: show the error, fix what is fixable within the skill's scope (for example an invalid task file, by re-running the `to-tasks` validation), or ask the user, then try again; never retry the same failing command unchanged. 5. *Never* run graph-execution without `--web` from the agent's shell, and never start a second run while one is live (check with `graph-execution open`) unless the user asks. - Copy the file to `.agents/skills/run-graph/SKILL.md` and `.claude/skills/run-graph/SKILL.md` so this repository's own agents have it (same as `to-tasks`). - **VALIDATE**: `npm test -- skills` ### EDIT `skills/to-tasks/SKILL.md` (and its two copies) - **IMPLEMENT**: replace the final paragraph of step 6 ("Finally, tell the user the tasks are ready and that they can run them with: …") by: *Tell the user the tasks are ready, show the command (`npx graph-execution .agents/tasks --spec --provider claude|codex|opencode|qwen`), and ask whether to start the run now. If they say yes and the `run-graph` skill is available, follow it; otherwise run the command with `--web` yourself, report the URL and stop.* Keep the rest unchanged. - **GOTCHA**: `src/install/skills.test.ts` asserts `validate-tasks.mjs .agents/tasks` and `.agents/tasks/.json` remain in the text; `.agents/skills/to-tasks` and `.claude/skills/to-tasks` must stay byte-identical to `skills/to-tasks`. - **VALIDATE**: `npm test -- skills` ### EDIT `src/install/skills.ts` - **IMPLEMENT**: `SKILLS_SOURCE = fileURLToPath(new URL("../../skills/", import.meta.url))`; list its subdirectories that contain a `SKILL.md` (sorted). Destinations become roots: `agents` → `.agents/skills`, `claude` → `.claude/skills`, `both` → both. For every (root, skill) pair: if the destination folder exists and `!force` → skipped; else (with `force`: `rm` it first) `cp` recursively → installed. Return `{ installed: string[]; skipped: string[] }` (absolute paths). Throw `InstallError(" already exists; nothing was installed (use --force to overwrite)")` only when nothing was installed and something was skipped, so the all-skipped case keeps its old message and exit code 2. - **VALIDATE**: `npm run typecheck` ### EDIT `src/cli.ts` - **IMPLEMENT**: description `Install the bundled skills (to-tasks, run-graph) into .agents/skills and/or .claude/skills`; print `Installed skill into ` per installed and `Skipped : already exists (use --force to overwrite)` per skipped (skipped lines to stdout when something was installed); the thrown `InstallError` covers the nothing-installed case. - **VALIDATE**: `npm test -- skills cli` ### EDIT `src/install/skills.test.ts` - **IMPLEMENT**: default install produces both `to-tasks` and `run-graph` under `.agents/skills`; target `claude`/`both`; second run refuses with `InstallError` and changes nothing; with `to-tasks` present only `run-graph` is installed and the result reports the skip; `--force` overwrites and removes stale files in both; replace the old "only one of two destinations exists" test by "installs what is missing and skips what exists" (both targets, `.claude/skills/to-tasks` exists → `.agents/skills/*` and `.claude/skills/run-graph` installed, `.claude/skills/to-tasks` skipped and untouched); a new "the bundled run-graph skill" test: frontmatter `name: run-graph` and a `description:` starting with `Start a graph-execution run`, mentions `--web`, exit codes `3` and `2`, the sentence not to sleep/poll, and `graph-execution open`; the CLI test prints one line per skill and exits 2 only when nothing was installed. - **VALIDATE**: `npm test -- skills` ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] `graph-execution install skills` installs `to-tasks` and `run-graph` into the chosen target(s); existing skill folders are skipped individually and reported with the `--force` hint; exit 2 only when nothing was installed and something was skipped. - [ ] `--force` overwrites every bundled skill folder and removes stale files. - [ ] `skills/run-graph/SKILL.md` has the specified frontmatter and the five steps, uses exit codes 0/2/3, and never tells the agent to monitor the run. - [ ] `to-tasks` ends by offering to start the run, with the `run-graph` fallback wording. - [ ] The three copies of each skill (`skills/`, `.agents/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`) are identical. - [ ] Tests pass: `npm test -- skills cli` ## Validation commands ```bash npm run typecheck && npm run lint npm test -- skills cli node skills/to-tasks/validate-tasks.mjs src/__fixtures__/diamond ```
